explanation: Found one accounting defect in the new same-transport lifetime boundary. Otherwise, source tracing confirms synchronous production dispatch, IP-before-Up retention, independent family updates, cleanup before acknowledgment, atomic accounting identity generation, and final transport teardown; the UDP assertion replacements and subprocess metric isolation do not weaken their stated proofs. No edits or validation were performed.

findings.title: Baseline accounting counters when starting a replacement lifetime
findings.body: `l2tpReactor.handleLCPDown` now ends accounting while retaining the PPP unit, and `radiusAcct.onSessionIPAssigned` creates a fresh accounting identity for its replacement. However, `radiusAcct.buildAcctPacket` still reports the entire `pppN` RX/TX byte and packet counters through `iface.GetStats`/`netlinkBackend.GetStats`; `pppSession.resetNCP` only disconnects the channel and removes NCP resources, without recreating the unit or resetting its counters. Consequently, if Alice transfers 100 MB and Bob authenticates on the retained transport, Bob's Stop includes Alice's 100 MB again, even if Bob transfers nothing. RFC 2866 §5.3 states: “This attribute indicates how many octets have been received from the port over the course of this service being provided, and can only be present in Accounting-Request records where the Acct-Status-Type is set to Stop.” Retain a counter baseline at the disconnected lifetime boundary and subtract it for replacement-lifetime octets, packets and gigawords, without resetting shared interface statistics. Extend the UDP replacement-lifetime proof with nonzero first-lifetime counters; its current empty `PppInterface` bypasses this path.
